title: Lesson 2: Multi-Tenant Platform Architecture: Orgs, Environments, and the Instance Model
description: Why every Salesforce org rents a slice of a shared platform: multi-tenancy, metadata-driven design, the instance model, and the sandbox environments that keep Dev/QA/UAT/Prod safe.

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: Why every Salesforce org rents a slice of a shared platform: multi-tenancy, metadata-driven design, the instance model, and the sandbox environments that keep Dev/QA/UAT/Prod safe.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: Here is the single fact that explains most of what surprises newcomers to Salesforce: you never own a server, a database, or even a schema.
You rent a private, configurable slice of a platform that thousands of other companies share.
This lesson makes the mechanism concrete, because the System Architect exam (and real architecture work) constantly assumes you understand it.
Almost every "weird" platform rule (governor limits, code-coverage gates, sandbox refresh windows, the instance your org lives on) is a direct consequence of that sharing.
